key_insight: Polystyrene can enhance initial shock heating at HMX pore interfaces, yet its subsequent heat-absorbing reactions inhibit hotspot growth and coalescence.
engineering_relevance: Explosive safety and initiation models should account for binder chemistry as well as pore geometry and mechanical response.
method: Reactive molecular dynamics of shock-induced void collapse in HMX.
Analysis of void-length effects, hotspot evolution, and polymer reactions.
evidence_signal: Simulations show void-length-dependent pressure–volume work, shock temperature, and reaction onset, followed by polymer chain scission and cross-bonding that suppress deflagration.
watch_item: The findings concern simulated HMX–polystyrene interfaces; applicability to other binders and experimental scales requires validation.
paper_title: Polymer-Mediated Hotspot Evolution in Shock-Induced Pore Collapse in 1,3,5,7-Tetranitro-1,3,5,7-tetrazocane (HMX)-based Explosives
